questions.prompt: Which statement about bacterial shapes is FALSE?

options.text: Spirochete describes a loose, flexible spiral.
Treponema pallidum is a spirochete that causes syphilis.

questions.explanation: False. Spirochete is a tight, rigid spiral; Spirillum is the loose spiral.

questions.prompt: A “diplococcus” arrangement means:
questions.explanation: A pair of round cells.

questions.prompt: Describe what flagella are made of, their function, and how they can contribute to disease.
questions.explanation: Flagella are made of protein, forming a complex rotary motor structure powered by a proton motive force; they’re used for motility. They contribute to disease by letting bacteria move toward and invade host tissue (e.g., H. pylori swimming through stomach mucus).

questions.prompt: Which statement about flagellar arrangements is FALSE?

options.text: Monotrichous = one flagellum at one end.
Lophotrichous = a tuft of flagella at one end.
Peritrichous = a single flagellum in the middle of the cell.

questions.explanation: False. Peritrichous means flagella distributed all around the cell, not a single central flagellum.

questions.prompt: Fimbriae are primarily used for:
questions.explanation: Adherence/attachment.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between fimbriae and a conjugation (sex) pilus, in terms of structure and function?
questions.explanation: Fimbriae are short protein filaments tipped with an adhesin, used for attachment to surfaces. A conjugation/sex pilus is a longer protein tube used to exchange genetic material (like plasmids) between cells in conjugation.

questions.prompt: A capsule is made primarily of:
questions.explanation: Carbohydrate.

questions.prompt: What is a biofilm, and what bacterial structure allows it to form? Give an example.
questions.explanation: A biofilm is a thin layer of bacteria adhered to a surface. The capsule (glycocalyx) allows bacteria to adhere and form biofilms — e.g., Streptococcus mutans forming a biofilm/plaque on teeth, causing cavities.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the bacterial cell wall is FALSE?

options.text: It protects against excessive water uptake.
All bacteria, without exception, have a cell wall.
Peptidoglycan is built from NAG and NAM sugar subunits.

questions.explanation: False. Mycoplasma naturally lacks a cell wall.

questions.prompt: The amino acid cross-links in peptidoglycan are important because they:

options.text: Give the cell wall rigidity/strength against osmotic pressure
Help the cell exchange genetic material

questions.explanation: Give the cell wall rigidity/strength against osmotic pressure.

questions.prompt: Describe the structure of the Gram-positive cell envelope.
questions.explanation: A thick layer of peptidoglycan studded with teichoic and lipoteichoic acids, surrounding a plasma membrane; no outer membrane.

questions.prompt: Describe the structure of the Gram-negative cell envelope.
questions.explanation: A thin layer of peptidoglycan, a plasma membrane beneath it, and an outer membrane containing lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and membrane proteins.

questions.prompt: Which statement about lysozyme and penicillin is FALSE?

options.text: Lysozyme is naturally found in tears and saliva.
Both lysozyme and penicillin ultimately weaken the cell wall, causing lysis.

questions.explanation: False. Penicillin inhibits new peptidoglycan cross-link formation (weakening the wall), it does not strengthen it.

questions.prompt: Bacteria with a waxy cell wall due to mycolic acid are called:
questions.explanation: Acid-Fast.

questions.prompt: Why is mycolic acid clinically relevant? Name at least two reasons.
questions.explanation: Mycolic acid confers resistance to phagocytosis, repels many antibiotics (harder to treat), and repels standard stains (requiring the Acid-Fast stain).

questions.prompt: Structurally, Acid-Fast bacteria most closely resemble:

options.text: Gram-negative bacteria, because both have an outer membrane
Gram-positive bacteria, because both lack an outer membrane and have a peptidoglycan layer
Mycoplasma, because both lack a cell wall
Archaea, because both live in extreme environments

questions.explanation: Gram-positive, because both lack an outer membrane and have a peptidoglycan layer (Acid-Fast just adds mycolic acid).

questions.prompt: Which genus of bacteria naturally lacks a cell wall?
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma.

questions.prompt: Why are cell-wall-targeting antibiotics ineffective against Mycoplasma infections?
questions.explanation: Cell-wall-targeting antibiotics have nothing to act on since Mycoplasma has no cell wall/peptidoglycan; effective drugs must target something else, which is often also present in human cells, raising toxicity concerns.

questions.prompt: Which pairing of organism to shape/arrangement or disease is FALSE?

options.text: Streptococcus pyogenes — chains of cocci — strep throat
Staphylococcus aureus — clusters of cocci — Staph infections
Helicobacter pylori — curved rod — stomach ulcers

questions.explanation: False. Mycobacterium tuberculosis is Acid-Fast (structurally similar to Gram-positive), not Gram-negative.

questions.prompt: Explain how the Gram stain works to distinguish Gram-positive from Gram-negative bacteria, and who developed it.
questions.explanation: The Gram stain, developed by Hans Christian Gram, is a differential stain that reveals cell envelope structure: bacteria with a thick peptidoglycan layer and no outer membrane (Grampositive) retain the stain and appear purple, while those with a thin peptidoglycan layer and an outer membrane (Gram-negative) do not retain it and appear pink.
